review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

17:1.sourceText: Διοδεύσαντες δὲ τὴν Ἀμφίπολιν καὶ τὴν Ἀπολλωνίαν ἦλθον εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, ὅπου ἦν συναγωγὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
17:1.targetText: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

groups.note: The participle Διοδεύσαντες ("having passed through") is rendered as a when-clause.
τῶν Ἰουδαίων ("of the Jews") is rendered Jewish.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed; When belongs to the participle.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:2.sourceText: κατὰ δὲ τὸ εἰωθὸς τῷ Παύλῳ εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς, καὶ ἐπὶ σάββατα τρία διελέξατο αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν,
17:2.targetText: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,

groups.note: The article τό, with τῷ Παύλῳ ("for Paul"), is rendered his custom.
αὐτούς ("them", the Jews of 17:1) is rendered the synagogue, where they met.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
πρός ("to") is absorbed into went into.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in As was his custom; κατὰ τὸ εἰωθός means "according to the custom".

17:3.sourceText: διανοίγων καὶ παρατιθέμενος ὅτι τὸν Χριστὸν ἔδει παθεῖν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός, ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ὃν ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
17:3.targetText: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. “This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ,” he declared.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB ends the sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
ὅτι introduces what Paul showed; BSB gives it as a direct quotation.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The relative ὅν ("whom") is left implicit in the English This Jesus I am proclaiming.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb of saying to introduce the quotation.

17:4.sourceText: καί τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπείσθησαν καὶ προσεκληρώθησαν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ, τῶν τε σεβομένων Ἑλλήνων πλῆθος πολὺ, γυναικῶν τε τῶν πρώτων οὐκ ὀλίγαι.
17:4.targetText: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.

groups.note: αὐτῶν ("them") is rendered the Jews.
The article with the participle σεβομένων ("worshiping") is rendered God-fearing.
οὐκ ὀλίγαι ("not a few") is rendered quite a few.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts the verse without rendering καί.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:5.sourceText: Ζηλώσαντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ προσλαβόμενοι τῶν ἀγοραίων ἄνδρας τινὰς πονηροὺς καὶ ὀχλοποιήσαντες ἐθορύβουν τὴν πόλιν, καὶ ἐπιστάντες τῇ οἰκίᾳ Ἰάσονος ἐζήτουν αὐτοὺς προαγαγεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον·
17:5.targetText: The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.

groups.note: τῶν ἀγοραίων ("the market people") is rendered from the marketplace.
ἄνδρας … πονηρούς ("wicked men") is rendered troublemakers.
καί, joining the participles, is rendered by the and of the English series.
ἐθορύβουν ("they were throwing into confusion") is rendered sent … into an uproar.
ἐζήτουν ("they were seeking") is rendered in search of.
αὐτούς ("them"), the object of προαγαγεῖν, is rendered them and is also named as Paul and Silas, whom they sought.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies hoping to carry the infinitive clause; ἐζήτουν ("they were seeking") is already rendered in search of.

17:6.sourceText: μὴ εὑρόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔσυρον Ἰάσονα καί τινας ἀδελφοὺς ἐπὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας, βοῶντες ὅτι Οἱ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀναστατώσαντες οὗτοι καὶ ἐνθάδε πάρεισιν,
17:6.targetText: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,

groups.note: The participle εὑρόντες ("having found") is rendered as a when-clause.
The article with the participle ἀναστατώσαντες ("those who upset") is rendered who have turned … upside down.

unmappedSource.reason: ὅτι introduces the quotation and is not separately expressed.
BSB leaves the adverbial καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds other to set the brothers apart from Jason.
English adds now; the Greek has the plain present πάρεισιν ("they are here").

17:7.sourceText: οὓς ὑποδέδεκται Ἰάσων· καὶ οὗτοι πάντες ἀπέναντι τῶν δογμάτων Καίσαρος πράσσουσιν, βασιλέα ἕτερον λέγοντες εἶναι Ἰησοῦν.
17:7.targetText: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”

groups.note: The relative οὕς ("whom") is rendered them, as BSB makes the relative clause a main clause.
ὑποδέδεκται ("has received as a guest") is rendered has welcomed … into his home.
ἀπέναντι … πράσσουσιν ("act contrary to") is rendered are defying; one of these words has a slightly different form in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB joins the relative clause οὓς ὑποδέδεκται Ἰάσων with and; the Greek has no conjunction there.
English introduces the reported statement; the Greek uses an infinitive.
English introduces the name; the Greek has no word for "name" here.

17:8.sourceText: ἐτάραξαν δὲ τὸν ὄχλον καὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας ἀκούοντας ταῦτα,
17:8.targetText: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.

groups.note: The active ἐτάραξαν ("they troubled") is rendered as passive were greatly disturbed.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:9.sourceText: καὶ λαβόντες τὸ ἱκανὸν παρὰ τοῦ Ἰάσονος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς.
17:9.targetText: And they collected bond from Jason and the others, and then released them.

groups.note: τὸ ἱκανόν ("the security") is rendered bond.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle λαβόντες, rendered they collected, to the main verb released.

17:10.sourceText: Οἱ δὲ ἀδελφοὶ εὐθέως διὰ νυκτὸς ἐξέπεμψαν τόν τε Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἰς Βέροιαν, οἵτινες παραγενόμενοι εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπῄεσαν·
17:10.targetText: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

groups.note: εὐθέως ("immediately") is rendered As soon as.
διὰ νυκτός ("by night") is rendered night had fallen.
The relative οἵτινες ("who") is rendered they, as BSB starts a new sentence.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The τε of τε καί ("both … and") is rendered only by the following and.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds there (Berea); the participle παραγενόμενοι means only arriving.

17:11.sourceText: οὗτοι δὲ ἦσαν εὐγενέστεροι τῶν ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ, οἵτινες ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον μετὰ πάσης προθυμίας, τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀνακρίνοντες τὰς γραφὰς εἰ ἔχοι ταῦτα οὕτως.
17:11.targetText: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.

groups.note: οὗτοι ("these") is rendered the Bereans.
τῶν ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ ("those in Thessalonica"), a genitive of comparison, is rendered than the Thessalonians.
The relative οἵτινες ("who, being such") gives the reason, rendered for they.

unmappedSource.reason: The article of τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ("daily") has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb of seeing to introduce the indirect question with if.
English joins the participle ἀνακρίνοντες, rendered examined, to the main verb received.

17:12.sourceText: πολλοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπίστευσαν, καὶ τῶν Ἑλληνίδων γυναικῶν τῶν εὐσχημόνων καὶ ἀνδρῶν οὐκ ὀλίγοι.
17:12.targetText: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.

groups.note: οὐκ ὀλίγοι ("not a few") is rendered quite a few.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:13.sourceText: Ὡς δὲ ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Θεσσαλονίκης Ἰουδαῖοι ὅτι καὶ ἐν τῇ Βεροίᾳ κατηγγέλη ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἦλθον κἀκεῖ σαλεύοντες καὶ ταράσσοντες τοὺς ὄχλους.
17:13.targetText: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.

groups.note: The passive κατηγγέλη ("was proclaimed") is rendered as active, with Paul as the subject.
κἀκεῖ ("there also") is rendered there themselves.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB makes Paul the subject of the active verb, so ὑπό ("by") has no English word.

17:14.sourceText: εὐθέως δὲ τότε τὸν Παῦλον ἐξαπέστειλαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πορεύεσθαι ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν· ὑπέμεινάν τε ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος ἐκεῖ.
17:14.targetText: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.

groups.note: ἕως ἐπί ("as far as") is rendered to.
θάλασσαν ("sea") is rendered coast.
The connective τε is rendered but.
ἐκεῖ ("there") is rendered in Berea.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
BSB leaves τότε ("then") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the infinitive πορεύεσθαι ("to go") untranslated; sent … to the coast carries it.
The τε of τε καί ("both … and") is rendered only by the following and.

17:15.sourceText: οἱ δὲ καθιστάνοντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον ἕως Ἀθηνῶν, καὶ λαβόντες ἐντολὴν πρὸς τὸν Σιλᾶν καὶ τὸν Τιμόθεον ἵνα ὡς τάχιστα ἔλθωσιν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐξῄεσαν.
17:15.targetText: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible.

groups.note: The article with the participle καθιστάνοντες ("those conducting") is rendered Those who escorted.
λαβόντες ("having received") is rendered with.
ὡς τάχιστα ("as quickly as possible") is rendered as soon as possible.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
πρός ("to") is absorbed into join.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for brought; τὸν Παῦλον is the object of the participle.

17:16.sourceText: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς Ἀθήναις ἐκδεχομένου αὐτοὺς τοῦ Παύλου, παρωξύνετο τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ θεωροῦντος κατείδωλον οὖσαν τὴν πόλιν.
17:16.targetText: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.

groups.note: The genitive absolute ἐκδεχομένου … τοῦ Παύλου is rendered While Paul was waiting for.
αὐτῷ ("him") is rendered as the subject he; BSB makes Paul, not his spirit, the one disturbed.
The genitive participle θεωροῦντος ("as he was seeing") is rendered to see.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB opens the new scene without rendering δέ; While belongs to the genitive absolute.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces what he saw with that; the Greek uses the participle οὖσαν ("being").

17:17.sourceText: διελέγετο μὲν οὖν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις καὶ τοῖς σεβομένοις καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν πρὸς τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας.
17:17.targetText: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.

groups.note: The article with the participle σεβομένοις ("those who worship") is rendered God-fearing.
κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν ("every day") is rendered each day.
The article with the participle παρατυγχάνοντας ("those happening by") is rendered those he met.

unmappedSource.reason: The particle μέν is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds Gentiles to identify the God-fearers; the Greek says only "the worshipers".

17:18.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἐπικουρίων καὶ Στοϊκῶν φιλοσόφων συνέβαλλον αὐτῷ, καί τινες ἔλεγον Τί ἂν θέλοι ὁ σπερμολόγος οὗτος λέγειν; οἱ δέ· Ξένων δαιμονίων δοκεῖ καταγγελεὺς εἶναι· ὅτι τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν εὐηγγελίζετο.
17:18.targetText: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
ἔλεγον ("they were saying") is rendered asked and is understood again with οἱ δέ, rendered said.
θέλοι ("would want") is rendered is … trying.
The noun καταγγελεύς ("proclaimer") is rendered advocating.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The particle ἄν has no English counterpart.
The connective δέ is not separately expressed; Others carries the contrast.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a frame for the explanation; the Greek has only ὅτι ("because").
English names the subject; the Greek gives him only in the verb ending of εὐηγγελίζετο.

17:19.sourceText: ἐπιλαβόμενοί δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν Ἄρειον πάγον ἤγαγον, λέγοντες Δυνάμεθα γνῶναι τίς ἡ καινὴ αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ σοῦ λαλουμένη διδαχή;
17:19.targetText: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different connective here; So renders either.
αὐτοῦ ("him") is rendered by the name Paul.
Ἄρειον πάγον ("Hill of Ares") is the Areopagus.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is rendered they asked.
The article with the passive participle λαλουμένη ("being spoken") is rendered that … are presenting.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB turns the passive into an active verb with you as subject, so ὑπό ("by") has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐπιλαβόμενοι, rendered took, to the main verb brought.
English supplies an object for brought; αὐτοῦ is the object of the participle.
English links the question to the Areopagus by place; the Greek has only the participle λέγοντες.
English supplies an object for asked.
English supplies a copula; the Greek question has no verb.

17:20.sourceText: ξενίζοντα γάρ τινα εἰσφέρεις εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν· βουλόμεθα οὖν γνῶναι τίνα θέλει ταῦτα εἶναι.
17:20.targetText: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears, and we want to know what they mean.”

groups.note: The connective οὖν ("so") is rendered and.
θέλει … εἶναι ("want to be") is rendered mean.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:21.sourceText: Ἀθηναῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες ξένοι εἰς οὐδὲν ἕτερον ηὐκαίρουν ἢ λέγειν τι ἢ ἀκούειν τι καινότερον.
17:21.targetText: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating new ideas.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἐπιδημοῦντες ("those staying") is rendered who lived.
ηὐκαίρουν εἰς ("they had leisure for") is rendered spent their time doing.
The connective ἤ ("or") is rendered and.
τι καινότερον ("something newer") is rendered new ideas.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB gives the object of both verbs once, as new ideas.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds there (Athens); ἐπιδημοῦντες means only staying.

17:22.sourceText: Σταθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ Ἀρείου Πάγου ἔφη Ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, κατὰ πάντα ὡς δεισιδαιμονεστέρους ὑμᾶς θεωρῶ.
17:22.targetText: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and said, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.

groups.note: μέσῳ ("midst") is rendered the meeting.
Ἀρείου Πάγου ("of the Hill of Ares") is the Areopagus.
Ἀθηναῖοι ("Athenians") is rendered of Athens.
ὡς ("as") introduces how Paul sees them, rendered that.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle Σταθείς, rendered stood up, to the main verb said.
English supplies a copula; the Greek has no verb in this clause.

17:23.sourceText: διερχόμενος γὰρ καὶ ἀναθεωρῶν τὰ σεβάσματα ὑμῶν εὗρον καὶ βωμὸν ἐν ᾧ ἐπεγέγραπτο ΑΓΝΩΣΤΩ ΘΕΩ. ὃ οὖν ἀγνοοῦντες εὐσεβεῖτε, τοῦτο ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν.
17:23.targetText: For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription:  TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.  Therefore what you worship as something unknown, I now proclaim to you.

groups.note: The participle διερχόμενος ("passing through") is rendered as I walked around.
ἐν ᾧ ("on which") is rendered with.
The pluperfect passive ἐπεγέγραπτο ("had been inscribed") is rendered this inscription.
The participle ἀγνοοῦντες ("not knowing") is rendered as something unknown.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the resumptive τοῦτο ("this") untranslated; what carries the object.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds now to mark the contrast; the Greek has the plain present καταγγέλλω ("I proclaim").
A participle has no person; English supplies I.

17:24.sourceText: ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ, οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων Κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ,
17:24.targetText: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands.

groups.note: The article with the participle ποιήσας ("the one who made") is rendered who made.
The participle ὑπάρχων ("being") is rendered is.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the resumptive οὗτος ("this one") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ὑπάρχων, rendered is, to the main verb live.

17:25.sourceText: οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος, αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα·
17:25.targetText: Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.

groups.note: The participle προσδεόμενος ("needing") is rendered as if He needed.
The participle διδούς ("giving") is rendered as a because-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:26.sourceText: ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,
17:26.targetText: From one man He made every nation of men, that they should inhabit the whole earth; and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.

groups.note: The infinitive κατοικεῖν ("to dwell") is rendered they should inhabit.
κατοικίας ("dwelling") is rendered lands.

ἐπί ("on") is absorbed into inhabit.
BSB leaves προσώπου ("face") untranslated: the whole earth.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the infinitive clause with that.
English joins the participle ὁρίσας, rendered He determined, to the main verb made.

17:27.sourceText: ζητεῖν τὸν Θεὸν, εἰ ἄρα γε ψηλαφήσειαν αὐτὸν καὶ εὕροιεν, καί γε οὐ μακρὰν ἀπὸ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου ἡμῶν ὑπάρχοντα.
17:27.targetText: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.

groups.note: The infinitive ζητεῖν ("to seek") continues the purpose of He made in 17:26.
Θεόν ("God") is the object of seek, rendered Him.
εἰ ἄρα γε ("if perhaps") is rendered perhaps.
αὐτόν ("him") is the object of both verbs; BSB repeats it after find.
καί γε ("and yet") is rendered though.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a frame; the Greek infinitive ζητεῖν depends on He made in 17:26.
English joins seek to reach out for; the Greek has εἰ ("if"), rendered with perhaps.

17:28.sourceText: ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ζῶμεν καὶ κινούμεθα καὶ ἐσμέν, ὡς καί τινες τῶν καθ’ ὑμᾶς ποιητῶν εἰρήκασιν Τοῦ γὰρ καὶ γένος ἐσμέν.
17:28.targetText: ‘For in Him we live and move and have our being.’ As some of your own poets have said, ‘We are His offspring.’

groups.note: ἐσμέν ("we are") is rendered have our being.
καθ’ ὑμᾶς ("among you") is rendered your own.
In the quoted line the article Τοῦ serves as the pronoun "his".

17:29.sourceText: γένος οὖν ὑπάρχοντες τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ὀφείλομεν νομίζειν, χρυσῷ ἢ ἀργύρῳ ἢ λίθῳ, χαράγματι τέχνης καὶ ἐνθυμήσεως ἀνθρώπου, τὸ Θεῖον εἶναι ὅμοιον.
17:29.targetText: Therefore, being offspring of God, we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by man’s skill and imagination.

groups.note: χαράγματι ("an engraved thing") is rendered an image formed.

17:30.sourceText: τοὺς μὲν οὖν χρόνους τῆς ἀγνοίας ὑπεριδὼν ὁ Θεὸς τὰ νῦν ἀπαγγέλλει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πάντας πανταχοῦ μετανοεῖν,
17:30.targetText: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times, He now commands all people everywhere to repent.

groups.note: τοὺς χρόνους τῆς ἀγνοίας ("the times of ignorance") is rendered the ignorance of … times.
The participle ὑπεριδών ("having overlooked") is rendered as an although-clause, set against τὰ νῦν ("now").
τὰ νῦν ("as for now") is rendered now.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
μὲν οὖν ("so then, on the one hand") is not separately expressed; Although belongs to the participle ὑπεριδών.
BSB follows a reading with a different verb here; N1904's ἀπαγγέλλει means "declares", not "commands".

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with a different verb here; commands does not render N1904's ἀπαγγέλλει ("declares").
English supplies the subject of the main verb; God is named in the first clause.
English adds earlier, setting those times against now; the Greek says "the times of ignorance".

17:31.sourceText: καθότι ἔστησεν ἡμέραν ἐν ᾗ μέλλει κρίνειν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ, ἐν ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὥρισεν, πίστιν παρασχὼν πᾶσιν ἀναστήσας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν.
17:31.targetText: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”

groups.note: ἐν ᾗ ("on which") is rendered when.

unmappedSource.reason: The relative ᾧ ("whom") is left implicit in the English the Man He has appointed.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds of this, referring to the coming judgment; the Greek has only πίστιν ("assurance").

17:32.sourceText: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν, οἱ μὲν ἐχλεύαζον, οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἀκουσόμεθά σου περὶ τούτου καὶ πάλιν.
17:32.targetText: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some began to mock him, but others said, “We want to hear you again on this topic.”

groups.note: The participle ἀκούσαντες ("having heard") is rendered as a when-clause.
The future Ἀκουσόμεθα ("we will hear") is rendered We want to hear.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed; When belongs to the participle.
The μέν … δέ contrast is expressed in English only by but.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated; again renders πάλιν.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for mock; ἐχλεύαζον has none.

17:33.sourceText: οὕτως ὁ Παῦλος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν.
17:33.targetText: At that, Paul left the Areopagus.

groups.note: οὕτως ("thus") is rendered At that.
μέσου αὐτῶν ("their midst") is rendered the Areopagus, the meeting Paul had addressed (17:22).

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
ἐκ ("out of") is absorbed into left.

17:34.sourceText: τινὲς δὲ ἄνδρες κολληθέντες αὐτῷ ἐπίστευσαν, ἐν οἷς καὶ Διονύσιος ὁ Ἀρεοπαγείτης καὶ γυνὴ ὀνόματι Δάμαρις καὶ ἕτεροι σὺν αὐτοῖς.
17:34.targetText: But some joined him and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.

groups.note: ἐν οἷς ("among whom") is rendered including.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render ἄνδρες ("men"); some covers the whole group.
BSB leaves the adverbial καί ("also") untranslated.
The καί between the names is rendered by a comma.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle κολληθέντες, rendered joined, to the main verb believed.
English turns σὺν αὐτοῖς ("with them") into a relative clause; the Greek has no relative or copula.
